responsibility: Compile an optimal-control problem from a spin system and a control structure. Context-generated drifts enter here; optimisation is a separate call.
contracts: control.drifts is a cell array over ensemble members, each containing a cell array over time: one generator for static drift or one per waveform point for time-dependent drift. Members have the same number of drift matrices. control.operators contains the generators multiplied by the waveform rows.

control.pulse_dt gives positive interval durations in seconds. For N intervals a rectangle waveform has N columns and a trapezium waveform has N+1 endpoint columns. Source and target lists contain square density matrices in zeeman-hilb and column vectors in the Liouville and wavefunction formalisms.

drifts() asks a context for unsummed systems and combines Hamiltonian, relaxation, and kinetics as H+1i*R+1i*K, including a supplied hydrodynamic contribution. mas_drifts() instead generates rotor-phase-resolved Hamiltonian stacks; it requires a uniformly weighted grid because the control ensemble uses an arithmetic mean.
change_guidance: Route new control fields through optimcon(): it consumes recognised fields and rejects leftovers. Decide whether a field is live per evaluation or frozen on workers. Re-run setup after changing generators, ensemble composition, or pool.

Preserve the distinction between general Liouville generators and paths that require Hermiticity: optimcon checks drift, control, and offset generators for Hilbert-space density matrices, wavefunctions, and the Goodwin method.

responsibility: Turn ensemble specifications into cases, evaluate each case on the worker holding its drift, and return mean fidelity and derivatives.
contracts: Catalog columns index state pair, drift, power, offset combination, phase-cycle row, and distortion row. Correlations restrict the Cartesian product; the budget selects a reproducible subset after correlation. Each selected case has equal weight.

optimcon() groups cases by drift index, stores common invariants and worker-specific drift slices in parallel.pool.Constant objects, and records the pool ID. ensemble() must use that pool context; a problem to be evaluated inside an external parfor is prepared there.

ens_block() rotates channel pairs and phases the states, adds offsets in Hz via 2*pi*offset*off_op, and scales the normalised waveform by the case power in rad/s before applying distortions. ensemble() reduces derivative sums and restores case order for individually returned trajectories.
change_guidance: Keep catalog construction, worker ownership, and final reordering consistent; compare single-case and multi-case results with distinct drifts or power levels.

Differentiate back to input coordinates through every waveform map. Apply the input freeze mask after these transformations; freezing a nominal X sample need not freeze the physical X sample after phase mixing or a temporal filter.

responsibility: Compute a single case's transfer fidelity and derivatives from forward states and backward costates for a prescribed physical waveform.
contracts: ens_block() selects grape_hilb for zeeman-hilb and grape_liouv for sphten-liouv, zeeman-liouv, and zeeman-wavef. The former evolves density matrices, the latter vectors. The target is on the conjugated side of the overlap; swapping it reverses the sign of the imaginary fidelity.

The gradient has the waveform shape; the Hessian indexes waveform(:) in MATLAB column order. 'real', 'imag', and 'square' take the real part, imaginary part, and squared modulus of an overlap. Average fidelity uses the post-interval nodes, not an integral weighted by interval length.

State-dependent trajectory penalties enter the physical fidelity and its backward costate here, not the waveform penalty list. Neither time-averaged fidelity nor trajectory penalties support Hessians. Rectangle and trapezium support first derivatives; ensemble Hessians require rectangle.
change_guidance: For a trapezium derivative, an interior sample contributes through both adjacent intervals; an endpoint contributes through only one. Check noncommuting controls, a multi-interval pulse, and numerical differences of the composed objective rather than a single propagator alone.
Keep formalism-specific boundaries: Liouville/wavefunction keyholes support first derivatives but not Newton/Goodwin Hessians; Hilbert-space rectangle keyhole Hessians are a distinct supported case.

responsibility: Map optimiser coordinates to normalised Cartesian controls and expose separate physical and waveform-penalty channels to the optimiser.
contracts: grape_xy() optionally expands coefficients using waveform*control.basis, obtains the ensemble fidelity, and appends the weighted waveform penalties. Penalties are evaluated on the expanded normalised waveform before case-specific power and distortion; each term has its own gradient/Hessian slice.

grape_phase() maps fixed amplitudes and variable phases into alternating X/Y rows, with one phase row per pair. grape_curv() accepts a per-point map and gradient pullback; grape_coop() accepts two stacked phase profiles for point-to-point transfer and penalises the squared norm of their combined off-target final states. These last two wrappers do not supply Hessians.

penalty() distinguishes norm (NS), derivative norm (DNS), componentwise spillout (SNS), and amplitude spillout (SNSA). SNSA tests the magnitude of each XY pair against scalar bounds; it is not equivalent to constraining the two components separately.
change_guidance: Return derivatives in the coordinates supplied by the optimiser, for every objective channel. A nonlinear reparameterisation needs its own chain-rule curvature for a Hessian; a gradient pullback alone is insufficient.
Keep freeze masks in the wrapper's input coordinates. Cartesian time-point freezing cannot be combined with a waveform basis; a cooperative mask has separate row blocks for the two pulses.

responsibility: Model the transfer from the programmed Cartesian waveform to the waveform delivered by the instrument.
contracts: Each row of control.distortion is an ensemble alternative; its columns are sequential stages. On a value-only call each stage returns a waveform; on a gradient call it must also return the Jacobian of output(:) with respect to input(:).

ens_block() accumulates stage Jacobians in forward composition order and applies the transpose to the physical waveform gradient. Nonidentity distortion callbacks are excluded from ensemble Hessian evaluation; control.distplot is a separate plotting path.
change_guidance: Use a filter or amplifier callback for a forward model; kernelest() estimates a convolution kernel from recorded input/output samples and is not itself a waveform callback. Check temporal cross-talk as well as simultaneous XY coupling with a directional finite difference.

responsibility: Maximise the assembled objective in the unfrozen coordinates, choose a search direction, and run the line search.
contracts: fmaxnewton(spin_system,cost_function,guess) vectorises the guess internally and returns its original shape. objeval reshapes trial points for the callback and maximises fidelity(1)-sum(fidelity(2:end)), with the same subtraction for gradient and Hessian channels.

'lbfgs' and 'rbfgs' use gradient history; 'rbfgs' forms and regularises a BFGS curvature matrix. 'newton' and 'goodwin' request the objective Hessian and regularise its negative on the unfrozen subspace. A zero-iteration request evaluates the value without taking a step.
change_guidance: Apply initial gradient and ascent-direction checks to the assembled, unfrozen objective, not to one physics or penalty term. Preserve that maximisation sign in bracketing, sectioning, and curvature updates; test a concave objective and opposing derivative contributions.

responsibility: Optimise slice durations at fixed field amplitudes, separately from the amplitude/phase ensemble wrappers.
contracts: tgrape() takes one Liouville-space drift, a control-by-slice physical waveform in rad/s, and a column of duration variables. It propagates for dt_grid*time_unit seconds and returns the real final target overlap and its gradient with respect to dt_grid, including the time_unit factor.
change_guidance: Put a total-duration constraint or lower bounds in the external optimiser, as in features_dt_opt; check derivatives by varying durations while holding amplitudes fixed, not by perturbing waveform samples.
